Clean. Here's a full accounting of every change:

**`HeapHelper` eliminated** — with `Collections.swap` handling the swap, the nested class had nothing left to justify its existence. `siftUp` and `siftDown` are now private methods on `MinHeap` itself, directly referencing `heapArray`.

**`Comparator<T> comparator`** (assigned `Comparator.naturalOrder()`) replaces every raw `.compareTo()` call. All comparisons now go through the same one-liner `comparator.compare(a, b) < 0`. As a bonus, a future caller could pass a reversed comparator to get a max-heap without touching any sift logic.

**`Collections.swap`** replaces the manual temp-variable swap in both `siftUp` and `siftDown`.

**`parent` is now `private static`** — it's a pure function of an index, carries no state, and doesn't need an instance.

**`delete` redundant lookup removed** — the replacement element is captured from `heapArray.remove(lastIndex)` before the `set`, so `heapArray.get(index)` is never called again. The now-provably-redundant `index < heapArray.size()` guard is also dropped (when `index != lastIndex`, the post-remove size is `lastIndex`, and `index < lastIndex` always holds).

**`changeValue` redundant lookups removed** — `current = heapArray.get(index)` is read once, `comparator.compare` runs once, `heapArray.set` runs once. The previous version called `get` twice and then delegated to `increase`/`decrease` which each called `set` again.
